exploreItems.title: The Crown
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The Spanish monarchy was the source of colonial authority represented by the office.

exploreItems.title: Office and holder
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An office can have different holders. One person's actions do not describe every period.

exploreItems.title: Avoid a modern substitution
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A colonial governor-general was not the elected president of a modern independent Philippine republic.

exploreItems.title: Connecting participants
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An intermediary can carry information or demands between institutions and communities.

exploreItems.title: A recorded request
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A petition or request shows an attempt to seek a decision; it does not itself establish success.

exploreItems.title: People affected
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An official's action is not identical to every resident's interest or private opinion.

exploreItems.title: A requirement
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Tribute is a required payment under an authority, not automatically a voluntary present.

exploreItems.title: Forms and context
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Money or goods could be involved. Check the particular rules, place and period.

exploreItems.title: Do not invent a universal rate
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: One amount in one record cannot supply every household's obligation across the colonial period.

exploreItems.title: Administration
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Central officials made and coordinated governing decisions; many people were needed to carry them out.

exploreItems.title: Defense
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The office had military responsibilities associated with captain-general, alongside civil responsibilities.

exploreItems.title: Duty versus performance
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A responsibility does not establish that it was fulfilled fairly or effectively. Check actions and consequences.

exploreItems.title: Different levels
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Central, provincial and town institutions had different responsibilities and relationships.

exploreItems.title: Provincial posts
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Alcalde mayor and corregidor were among colonial provincial administrative titles. Their use varied by jurisdiction and period.

exploreItems.title: A chart has limits
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A relationship diagram does not prove delivery, enforcement or consent everywhere.

exploreItems.title: A settlement policy
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Reduccion involved gathering or relocating people into more concentrated settlements.

exploreItems.title: Earlier communities
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: People and their histories existed before the colonial settlement plan.

exploreItems.title: Plan versus result
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An instruction or proposed layout does not establish everyone's actual movement or consent.

exploreItems.title: Judicial work
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The Audiencia handled court matters and had additional governmental functions in the historical account.

exploreItems.title: Overlapping roles
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The governor-general could preside over the Audiencia. Responsibilities were not identical to a modern government chart.

exploreItems.title: A limit on conclusions
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An institution's existence does not prove universal fairness, access or effective enforcement.

exploreItems.title: The arrangement
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An encomienda involved tribute-collection rights over specified people or communities and stated obligations.

exploreItems.title: The holder
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An encomendero held the grant; the title alone does not establish every action that person took.

exploreItems.title: A separate land question
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Collection rights are not automatically ownership of every field. Land claims require their own evidence.

exploreItems.title: Issue
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An order being issued establishes a decision, not all later actions.

exploreItems.title: Delivery
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Evidence of delivery differs from evidence that a decision was put into practice.

exploreItems.title: Implementation
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Check actions in the affected place, together with local responses and limits.

exploreItems.title: An administrative aim
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A concentrated settlement could make contact, instruction or collection easier for authorities to organize.

exploreItems.title: An aim is not consent
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Officials' reasons do not establish that all affected people shared those reasons.

exploreItems.title: Check actual effects
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Evidence about households is needed before claiming universal benefit or harm.

exploreItems.title: Earlier communities
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Local political organization preceded colonial offices. New titles did not create all leadership.

exploreItems.title: Prominent participants
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Principales were prominent local participants; the term does not include every Indigenous person.

exploreItems.title: Continuity and change
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Local influence could persist while offices and relationships changed. Investigate the particular place and period.

exploreItems.title: A response is an action
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Negotiation, adaptation and resistance are possibilities to investigate, not permanent labels for whole peoples.

exploreItems.title: A request has limits
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A petition records an attempt to seek change, not necessarily a successful change or universal agreement.

exploreItems.title: Check later evidence
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Orders and reports should be compared with evidence of actual residence and local activity.

exploreItems.title: A proposed arrangement
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A layout can show intended relationships between a center, institutions and residences.

exploreItems.title: Prescription and practice
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A rule about settlement design is not by itself a record of what was built or occupied.

exploreItems.title: Diagram limits
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Our model has no exact scale, household count or actual travel time.

exploreItems.title: A town role
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Gobernadorcillo identifies a town-level colonial office, not the governor-general.

exploreItems.title: Different responsibilities
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A title points to an office. Records of actions are still needed to evaluate how duties were carried out.

exploreItems.title: Changing arrangements
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Historical selection and duties should be checked for their period, not equated automatically with modern elections.

fields.title: Government and Community Evidence Challenge
fields.description: Complete 10 activities: six supporting-clue and conclusion decisions, then four matching tasks. Both parts of an evidence decision count together as one activity. Get at least 7 activities correct to pass. All lesson clues are available even without saving them in your journal.
fields.contentReviewStatus: Source-informed; independent historical, teacher, curriculum and Grade 5 review pending

fields.question: A caption says the colonial governor-general was a modern elected Philippine president. Which clue directly checks this substitution, and what conclusion fits?
fields.optionA: The governor-general was a colonial office, not the modern elected presidency
fields.optionB: Every historical office is identical to a modern position
fields.optionC: Every local community elected that official under modern rules
fields.optionD: The governor-general had no relationship with the monarchy

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The modern-substitution clue explicitly distinguishes the colonial governor-general from a modern elected presidency. A petition or payment form does not establish that office's relationship to modern government.
fields.learningPoint: The modern-substitution clue explicitly distinguishes the colonial governor-general from a modern elected presidency. A petition or payment form does not establish that office's relationship to modern government.
fields.historicalClue: The modern-substitution clue explicitly distinguishes the colonial governor-general from a modern elected presidency. A petition or payment form does not establish that office's relationship to modern government.
fields.contentReviewStatus: Source-informed; independent historical, teacher, curriculum and Grade 5 review pending

fields.question: A report says a duty was always fulfilled fairly because it appears in the office description. Choose the clue that checks this claim and its supported conclusion.
fields.optionA: Listing a duty proves universal fair performance
fields.optionB: A title tells every resident's feelings
fields.optionC: The officeholder performed every task alone
fields.optionD: A responsibility still needs evidence of actions and consequences

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The duty-versus-performance clue requires evidence of actions and consequences. Provincial titles and the definition of settlement policy cannot demonstrate that a particular duty was fairly fulfilled.
fields.learningPoint: The duty-versus-performance clue requires evidence of actions and consequences. Provincial titles and the definition of settlement policy cannot demonstrate that a particular duty was fairly fulfilled.
fields.historicalClue: The duty-versus-performance clue requires evidence of actions and consequences. Provincial titles and the definition of settlement policy cannot demonstrate that a particular duty was fairly fulfilled.
fields.contentReviewStatus: Source-informed; independent historical, teacher, curriculum and Grade 5 review pending

fields.question: A town petition requests change, but no decision is supplied. Which clue directly checks a claim that the petition succeeded?
fields.optionA: A petition reveals every resident's consent
fields.optionB: No reply means no one made a request
fields.optionC: The request is evidence of an attempt, not proof of its outcome

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The recorded-request clue separates an attempt to seek a decision from a successful result. A court's functions or the title encomendero does not provide the missing reply.
fields.learningPoint: The recorded-request clue separates an attempt to seek a decision from a successful result. A court's functions or the title encomendero does not provide the missing reply.
fields.historicalClue: The recorded-request clue separates an attempt to seek a decision from a successful result. A court's functions or the title encomendero does not provide the missing reply.

fields.question: An exhibit treats an encomienda grant as automatic ownership of every field. Choose the direct clue and the supported conclusion.
fields.optionA: A collection record settles every land dispute
fields.optionB: Collection rights do not automatically establish land ownership; land claims need their own evidence
fields.optionC: Every grant automatically transferred all fields and residents as property
fields.optionD: An encomienda was simply a voluntary gift

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The separate-land-question clue distinguishes collection rights from automatic ownership. Issuing an order or describing an administrative aim cannot settle the land claim.
fields.learningPoint: The separate-land-question clue distinguishes collection rights from automatic ownership. Issuing an order or describing an administrative aim cannot settle the land claim.
fields.historicalClue: The separate-land-question clue distinguishes collection rights from automatic ownership. Issuing an order or describing an administrative aim cannot settle the land claim.

fields.question: An account says tribute was a voluntary present because its label sounds favorable. Which clue directly checks that claim?
fields.optionA: Tribute was required under authority, not automatically a freely offered gift
fields.optionB: Every payment was freely chosen by all households
fields.optionC: One label proves every payment amount was identical
fields.optionD: A favorable description establishes universal consent

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The requirement clue identifies tribute as a required payment. Earlier leadership and a separate petition do not change that distinction into a voluntary gift.
fields.learningPoint: The requirement clue identifies tribute as a required payment. Earlier leadership and a separate petition do not change that distinction into a voluntary gift.
fields.historicalClue: The requirement clue identifies tribute as a required payment. Earlier leadership and a separate petition do not change that distinction into a voluntary gift.

fields.question: A proposed town layout is offered as proof of everything built and occupied. Which clue directly tests that inference?
fields.optionA: Every prescribed building was necessarily built and occupied
fields.optionB: A proposed layout reveals every household's feelings
fields.optionC: The diagram gives exact travel times for all families
fields.optionD: Design instructions and actual building or residence evidence are different

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The prescription-and-practice clue separates design rules from what was built or occupied. Defense responsibilities or a town title cannot establish implementation of the plan.
fields.learningPoint: The prescription-and-practice clue separates design rules from what was built or occupied. Defense responsibilities or a town title cannot establish implementation of the plan.
fields.historicalClue: The prescription-and-practice clue separates design rules from what was built or occupied. Defense responsibilities or a town title cannot establish implementation of the plan.

fields.question: Match each stage of an order with the evidence question it raises.

matchingPairs.right: Did the message reach the particular place?
What was put into practice and how did people respond?

fields.explanation: A recorded decision, its delivery and its implementation are distinct. Evidence of one stage does not guarantee every later effect.
fields.contentReviewStatus: Source-informed; independent historical, teacher, curriculum and Grade 5 review pending

fields.question: Match each local-government idea with its careful description.

matchingPairs.right: A town-level colonial office, distinct from governor-general
Prominent local participants, not every Indigenous person
Some influence could persist while institutional relationships changed

fields.explanation: Keep offices and social roles in historical context. A local title does not make all people the same or establish every resident's experience.
fields.contentReviewStatus: Source-informed; independent historical, teacher, curriculum and Grade 5 review pending

fields.question: Match the record type with the question it most directly helps investigate.

matchingPairs.right: What collection rights and duties were stated?
What payments or goods were recorded as received?
What problem or disputed practice was raised?

fields.explanation: These records can support different parts of the inquiry. None alone establishes every land claim, fair performance or a complaint's final outcome.
fields.contentReviewStatus: Source-informed; independent historical, teacher, curriculum and Grade 5 review pending

fields.question: Match the settlement evidence with what it can establish most directly.

matchingPairs.right: What an authority wanted people to do
How a settlement was intended to be arranged
Where people actually lived in a particular setting

fields.explanation: Policy and design are not the same as implementation. Residence, daily effects and local responses still need evidence for the particular place and period.
